text:
marta: Heads up — main/serving-tests is red again on CI. Failing test: test_stream_order_fuzzy. Looks nondeterministic, only observed on linux and aarch64 runners so far. cc @sam @li

ci-bot: Job failed: https://ci.redwood.example/job/serving-tests/4521/console (artifact: logs/serving/test_stream_order_fuzzy/98432.txt) :exclamation:
```
AssertionError: expected order [A, B, C] but got [A, C, B]
 at runtime/stream/reorderer.go:214
Stack: ... Reorderer.process -> Reorderer.maybeFlush -> assertSequence
```

sam: Can you paste the failing seed and the full reproduce command? Does it repro locally for you?

marta: Repro command I used: `TEST_SEED=98432 pytest -k test_stream_order_fuzzy -q -s --maxfail=1`
It repros locally ~1/30 runs on my linux devbox. On mac it hasn't reproduced. I also saw a different seed yesterday: 98550.

li: This smells like a scheduling/timer race in the windowing code. Two quick asks: (1) can we collect a bunch of failing seeds by doing a 100-run stress on CI? (2) try running with `--capture=no` and `GODEBUG=schedtrace=100` to see goroutine scheduling spikes.

jordan: I can spin a linux-x86 runner and run 500 iterations overnight if you want. Want me to do that or should we ask infra to run on the dedicated stress pool?

marta: If you can run 500 that'd be great. I'll open an ephemeral queue slot. Also: here's the small log snippet from the failing run showing timestamps are close: `received at 12:03:14.123`, `flushed at 12:03:14.124` — ordering depended on microsecond jitter.

anna: Short-term mitigation: add a defensive stable-sort by arrival timestamp in the reorderer so tests (and production) don't see reordering just because of scheduling jitter. Long-term we should make the test seed the clock or use a deterministic mock clock.

qa-bot: Suggestion: label this test `type:flaky` and add to the flaky-tests board: https://boards.redwood.example/flaky-tests (auto-suggested) :clipboard:

sam: I'll kick off a 100-run CI rerun now and capture seeds that fail. Command: `./scripts/ci-rerun --job serving-tests --test test_stream_order_fuzzy --runs 100 --collect-seeds`

ci-bot: Rerun started (job 4532). Will post summary when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(20m later)

ci-bot: Rerun finished. 100 runs, 4 failures. Seeds: 98432, 98470, 98501, 98550. Failed on runners: linux-x86-64 (3) and aarch64 (1). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/job/serving-tests/4532/artifacts/

li: Thanks — I'll start a bisect across the commit range (main~20..main) focusing on changes touching runtime/stream and allocator. If someone can confirm whether any recent allocator timing patches touched timestamps, that'd narrow it.

marta: Git sha at head when failing: `a1b2c3d4` (the usual main). The seeds above reproduce consistently with the CI artifacts attached.

li: Bisect update: narrowed down to commit `f9e4b2c` which changed the windowing flushing behaviour and touched reorderer ordering heuristics. Reverting that commit locally plus stress-run eliminated failures in 200 iterations.

sam: Nice. Can you propose a small fix/guard so we don't need to revert? If a guard is trivial we can hotfix and run another stress.

li: Proposed patch: ensure `Reorderer.flush()` uses stable sort by `createdAt` when sequence numbers are equal, and add an invariant check in tests that logs the seed on assertion. I'll draft a PR.

marta: Please include the failing seeds in the test output and add a harness flag `--record-seed-on-fail`. I'll open the github issue/PR and reference this thread.

jordan: I ran the overnight 500-run too — results align with CI seeds. No new seeds beyond the four. Happy to validate the patch once you put up a PR.

marta: Thanks all. Assigning follow-ups: @li will open PR, @sam will run a 500-run smoke once PR lands, @anna will add deterministic-clock note to the test TODO. I'll file the flaky issue and attach artifacts. :thumbsup:

qa-bot: Created issue #1423: "Flaky: test_stream_order_fuzzy — nondeterministic ordering under timer jitter" and linked artifacts.

marta: Closing loop here — will monitor next 24h after PR. If anyone observes new seeds ping this thread.
